summary: A guide to finding and using mental health services, covering how to talk to parents, recognizing signs that help is needed, types of services, barriers to access, and how to choose a provider. It includes expert comments from Sarah Peterson, Rachel Stein and Anthony Miller, plus a NAMI anti-stigma campaign. It closes with advice on self-care, involving loved ones, and patience during trial and error.
one_line: A guide to navigating mental health services, from recognizing the need for help and choosing providers to overcoming access barriers and practicing self-care.
key_facts: On September 5, 2023, Sarah Peterson, a licensed clinical psychologist based in Minneapolis, shared insights on approaching parents or guardians about the need for mental health support.
Sarah Peterson says "Preparation is key" and advises people to arm themselves with information about what they are experiencing and the types of help available.
Rachel Stein, a school counselor at Westdale High School, led a seminar on mental wellness on October 10, 2023.
Rachel Stein lists increasing isolation, changes in eating or sleeping patterns, and prolonged feelings of sadness or irritability as possible signals that someone needs help.
As of November 1, 2023, service options include individual therapy, group therapy, psychiatric services, online counseling, and support groups.
Psychiatric services are for those who may need medical intervention; psychiatrists can provide diagnoses and prescribe medications.
On December 8, 2023, the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) launched a campaign to reduce the stigma of mental health care, including a database of affordable services.
Sliding scale fees, teletherapy, and community mental health centers can make services more accessible, and the Crisis Text Line offers immediate help at no cost.
Local directories, online databases like Psychology Today, and recommendations from primary care physicians or school counselors are suggested for finding providers.

Anthony Miller, an advocate with the Mental Health Services Administration, suggests checking credentials and meeting potential therapists to gauge comfort and compatibility, saying "There has to be a good fit."
The guide says not every therapist or treatment modality will resonate with everyone, so patience and ongoing feedback with the provider are crucial.
Self-care recommendations include regular exercise, a healthy diet, enough sleep, and stress management such as meditation or yoga.
Involving family or close friends can add support, but setting boundaries around their involvement is important.
